en.title: Sum of the Longest Subarray Lengths Covered by Each Maximum
en.description:
For each position i in the array, find the length of the longest contiguous subarray that contains i and has a[i] as its maximum, forming an array b. Output the sum of all elements of b. The subarray may contain other maxima equal to a[i].

The standard input/output, the ranges added by this site, and the examples follow this problem's description; wherever the source's ranges are missing, they are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n (this site's addition: 1≤n≤100000); the second line contains n integers (this site's addition: −10^9≤a[i]≤10^9). The original snapshot only gives n≤10^5 and no element range; the answer is output as a 64-bit integer.
en.output: Output the sum of the longest subarray lengths over all positions, stored as a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: For each position, find the nearest strictly greater element on the left and on the right. Every element between them is no greater than the current value, so the maximum valid range length is the width between the two boundaries. Use a monotonic stack to find the boundaries in linear time.
